APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF DECEMBER 6, 2022

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:07 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Alma D. Puente, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Martin R. Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – absent

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  Items 13.11 and 13.12 have been pulled

4.  REGULAR AGENDA:

  4.1  Consideration and Approval of a Resolution of the City Council of the City of El
  Monte, California Reciting the Fact of the City of El Monte’s November 8, 2022
  General Municipal and Other Related Matters and Declaring the Results of Said
  Election. Installation of newly elected officials and selection of Mayor Pro
  Tempore.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Approve the attached Resolution reciting the fact of the City’s November 8,
  2022 General Municipal Election and other related matters and declaring the
  results of said election in compliance with Elections Code Sections 10263 and
  10264.
  2. Following approval of Resolution, the City Clerk shall issue the oath of office to
  all newly elected/re-elected officials and said officials shall be installed to office.
  3. The incoming City Council shall select one of its members to serve as Mayor
  Pro Tempore.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No.: N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  IMPORTANT NOTE: As of the publication of this agenda, the City Clerk is not in
  receipt of the final canvass of election results issued by the Registrar
  Recorder/County Clerk for the County of Los Angeles. It is anticipated, but not
  guaranteed, that the canvass will be received by close of business on December
  5, 2022. In the event said document is not receive by the City Clerk by the start
  of the City Council meeting, this item will be continued to a special meeting or the
  next available regular meeting.
  Resolution No. 10414

  Table item
   City Council Meeting Minutes of December 6, 2022

5.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete all
  Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council completes
  all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short recess
  and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event the City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by 7:00
  p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting,
  immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public wish to
  address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City Council shall
  allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed on page
  1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed session; and (ii) be
  subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total per
  speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Item 5.1 through 5.3.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
  6:33 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:28 p.m.

  Assistant City Attorney Lloyd Pilchen reported out of Closed Session with respect
  to Items 5.1 through 5.3.

  5.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54956.9(d)(1) – Existing
  Litigation – E. Gonzalez vs. City of El Monte, WC Case #ADJ14172981.

  Reports provided by legal counsel and staff, no reportable final action taken.

  5.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54956.9(d)(1) – Existing
  Litigation – M. Paredes vs. City of El Monte, WC Case #ADJ16448146.

  Reports provided by legal counsel and staff, no reportable final action taken.

  5.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiators.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721); El Monte Police
  Officers Association; El Monte Police Mid-Manager’s Association; and All
  Unrepresented Employees of City Executive Team.

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma Martinez, City Manager.

  Reports provided by legal counsel and staff, no reportable final action taken.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

9.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under
  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments
  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

  Marco Hernandez – Here regarding the last meeting regarding the street vendors. Have
  not gotten any conclusion regarding the removal of street vendors.

  Martin Garcia – Here regarding the last meeting regarding receiving support from the City.
  We have not received anything yet. Want the City to remove the street vendors.

  Moises Castañeda – Requesting respect. The City continues to make promises, and
  nothing has happened.

  Rogelio Ahundiz – My restaurant is located here at Valley Mall. Our sales are very low
  due to the street vendors. There have been some incidents caused because of the
  vendors. We are tasking for your help.

  Erika Mesa – Owner of a restaurant in the City and I agree with everyone economically.
  The City will be struggling economically if the businesses start closing one by one.

  Manuel Estrada – We are here because we are asking for your help. Our sales have gone
  down and we do not believe the City is being jus

  Lawrence Ou – The street vendors are affecting my sales. Please help us.

  Willie Rodriguez – I believe that the street vendors issue should be at the top of your list.
  Our businesses are being affected by this.

  Humberto Navarro – We have been coming here for two years and nothing has been
  done.

  David Ma – I am here talking about the same issue. I came here about 6 months ago and
  nothing has been done.

  Jesus Sandoval – I am here to ask the Council some questions. I don’t understand why
  the City doesn’t help us. Why is the City helping out the street vendors.

  Lyndon Dieu – Here to speak about the issues arising from the street vendors near my
  neighborhood. The street vendors are obstructing the view which will someday cause an
  accident.

  Alberto Grajeda – I am just here to speak about the issues arising from the street vendors.
  I have had on many occasions to clean after the street vendors. There are many times
  that vehicles are obstructing our driveway.

  Gabriela Caro – Spoke about the illegal hedges that are obstructing the view.

  Julio Ramirez – Spoke about the Street Vendors Ad Hoc Members. Also spoke about the

  Miguel Alvillar – Spoke about the street vendor issues that have been going on for years

  Mike Gomez – Spoke about his removal from the Measure EM Committee.

  Jerry Velasco – Spoke about the need for respect.

  Mary Ann Powers – Spoke about the street vendor issues. Something needs to be done.

  Cosme Jimenez – Spoke about respect, former Mayor and former Councilmembers.

  19A.  Mayor Ancona

  Not necessarily want to clear all the commissions since there is institutional
  knowledge. Would like to phase people out and we could fill those positions.
  There is the Human Relations Ad Hoc Commission that will require
  appointments. As this opens up we can start appointing from districts.

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of December 6, 2022

  There is a large need in our veteran commission. We should revisit the
  Veterans Affairs Commission.

  Reminder the Oath Office Ceremony will be this Saturday at the Grace T.
  Black Auditorium beginning at 9:00 am.

  Wish everyone Happy Holidays and Happy New Year.

19B.  Mayor Pro Tem Puente

  Just wanted to bring up to consider and discuss the possibility of clearing
  commissions and appointing in some fashion, based on Districts that there
  is equitable representation.

19C.  Councilman Herrera

  Spoke about the request being proposed for funding for the Veterans.

  Mentioned that the City Attorney’s Office will be making a presentation
  regarding the Commissions and Committees. The City Clerk was asked to
  prepare a list of the members serving on each of these committees and

19D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  19D.1 Discussion and Action Regarding Support for Veterans Utility Grants.

  At the Veteran’s Day event was approached by one of the World War
  II Veterans who mentioned that the City should have a Water Fund
  that supports some of the Veterans’ needs.

  Would like to see a utility grant program to support some of the
  elderly veterans.

  19D.2 Requested Update and Discussion on Street Vendor Policies.

  What is the plan to deal with street vendors. We should revisit the
  outdoor dining.

  19D.3 Discussion and Action on Re-Allocation of ARPA Funding to Support
  Recovering El Monte Small Businesses.

  Some of the businesses have hit a rail in getting utility bills that are
  high paid. Relaunch a marketing plan with regards to the grant
  programs available for veterans and small businesses. Reallocate
  some ARPA funds for small businesses.

  Merry Christmas, Happy Hannukah, have a blessed New Year.
  Congratulations to the newly elected.

19E.  Councilwoman Dr. Morales
